tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Your hypothesis is right, but the leak only happens when no type filter is active.

**How results are built**
1. When the modal opens, [NodeSearchModal.tsx:411](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSearchModal.tsx:411) calls `QueryEngine.getDiscourseNodeCandidates()` once.
2. [QueryEngine.ts:78-91](apps/obsidian/src/services/QueryEngine.ts:78) asks `getFilesWithNodeTypeId()` for files. That's the Datacore query `@page and exists(nodeTypeId)`, or the vault-scan fallback at `:715`, which checks the same thing. The loader then keeps any file whose `nodeTypeId` is a non-empty string. **Nothing checks that string against `plugin.settings.nodeTypes`.**
3. On each keystroke, `rankDiscourseNodesByTitle` → `filterCandidatesByNodeTypeIds` ([QueryEngine.ts:793](apps/obsidian/src/services/QueryEngine.ts:793)) treats an empty selection as "no filter". `fromPanelSelectedIds` also turns "all types checked" into an empty selection. So in the default state, invalid ids pass straight through. Picking only some types does hide them, which is probably why this slipped past.
4. The modal already handles these rows: [NodeSearchModal.tsx:478](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSearchModal.tsx:478) gives unknown ids an "Unknown type" fallback badge. That's the symptom you saw in the Loom.

The repo already has the check we need: [fileChangeListener.ts:103](apps/obsidian/src/utils/fileChangeListener.ts:103) uses `getNodeTypeById(plugin, nodeTypeId)` to decide whether a file is a node. The tag-candidate loader `getCandidateNodes(nodeTypes)` also only produces configured types, so it isn't affected.

## Plan

**Fix (one place, at load time)**
- Change `getDiscourseNodeCandidates` to take `nodeTypes: DiscourseNode[]`, the same way `getCandidateNodes` does. It builds a `Set` of the configured ids and skips any file whose `nodeTypeId` isn't in it.
- In the modal, pass `plugin.settings.nodeTypes` and add it to that effect's deps, like the tag-candidate effect. A type deleted while the modal is open then drops out too.
- `getFilesWithNodeTypeId` stays as it is. It has other callers, and Datacore can't see plugin settings.

**Tests** (in the existing `services/__tests__/QueryEngine.test.ts`)
- Configured types are kept. An unknown id, an empty string and a non-string value are all dropped.
- Cover both the Datacore path and the vault-scan fallback, since both feed the same loop.

**Verification**
- `pnpm -C apps/obsidian test`, plus typecheck and lint.
- Live check with `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`. In `testVault123`, create a note with `nodeTypeId: bogus`, open advanced search with no filter and confirm it's gone while real nodes still show. Before trusting the run, grep the copied bundle for the new code, because other worktrees' dev watchers write to the same vault.

**Proposed Done When** (the ticket's is empty)
- Advanced node search only lists files whose `nodeTypeId` matches a configured node type, whatever the type filter is set to.
- Unit tests cover unknown, empty and non-string `nodeTypeId`.

## Open questions
1. **"Unknown type" badge fallback:** after the fix, nothing should reach it. Should I keep it as a harmless guard (my lean, since your rules say not to remove things unprompted) or delete it as dead code?
2. **Imported nodes:** imports map `nodeTypeId` to a local type ([importNodes.ts:1722](apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1722)). If an imported note's type was never mapped, it disappears from search after this fix. Is that what you want, or should imported nodes be exempt?

Should I go ahead and fill in Done When on the ticket, then implement?

content.text:
It didn't. The tag scan is fine. Two loaders have confusingly similar names, and I made it worse by calling both "candidate" in my summary.

| Loader | Added in | What it scans | What it returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getDiscourseNodeCandidates()` | ENG-2108 (`0ce17769`), when the search modal was first built | Files with a `nodeTypeId` in frontmatter | **Existing nodes**, the default result pool |
| `getCandidateNodes(nodeTypes)` | ENG-2272 (`a1c1d0af`) | The metadata cache's tag index only | **Candidate nodes**: tagged lines, shown only when the toggle is on |

In the first loader, "candidate" means *something in the pool the search ranks*, not *a candidate node*. `DiscourseNodeCandidate` is the type for one entry in that pool. ENG-2272 reused the type and added an optional `tagLine` field to mark the tagged-line results. As a result, "candidate" now means two different things in `QueryEngine.ts`.

That changes the history of the bug, not the fix:
- **The leak is in the existing-node loader, and it dates back to ENG-2108.** Any file with a non-empty `nodeTypeId` has been in the default results since the modal shipped. It only got noticed during the ENG-2272 Loom tests.
- **The tag scan is fine.** `getCandidateNodes` builds its map from `nodeTypes` and only keeps tags that match a configured type, so it can't return an unknown type.

So the plan stays the same: check `getDiscourseNodeCandidates` against the configured node types. One thing to add: the ticket and PR should say the bug comes from ENG-2108, not ENG-2272, so nobody goes looking in the tag code.

On the naming: renaming `getDiscourseNodeCandidates` / `DiscourseNodeCandidate` to something like `getSearchableNodes` / `SearchableNode` would clear this up. It touches the modal, the sort helpers and the tests, though, so I'd file it as its own small ticket rather than fold it into this fix. Want me to draft that ticket, or go ahead with the fix as planned?

content.text:
Yes, imported notes will stay. Here's how I checked.

**Why imported notes pass the check**
- During import, `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` ([importNodes.ts:1246-1308](apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts:1246)) either matches the remote type to a local one by id or name, or **adds the imported type to `plugin.settings.nodeTypes`** with `importedFromRid` set.
- It then writes the mapped id into the note's frontmatter (`:1778`).
- The type filter panel builds its list from that same `plugin.settings.nodeTypes` (`NodeSearchModal.tsx:613,622`). Imported types already show up there, and the new check reads the same list, so imported notes stay in the results.

One edge case: if the remote schema can't be fetched at import time, `mapNodeTypeIdToLocal` returns the raw source id without registering a type (`:1240`). The same happens if someone later deletes an imported type. Those notes have a type no settings entry knows, so under your rule they drop out. I think that's right, but I'll call it out in the PR.

## What changes in the plan

**Unknown types are removed completely:**
- Delete the "Unknown type" fallback in `NodeSearchModal.tsx:478`. If a row's type isn't in `nodeTypesById`, the modal drops the row. This only kicks in when settings change between load and render.
- Delete `getFallbackNodeTypeBadge` from `utils/nodeTypeBadge.ts`. The modal is its only caller and it has no tests.

**Unchanged from the last plan:**
1. Rename commit:
   - `getDiscourseNodeCandidates` → `getSearchableNodes(nodeTypes)`
   - `DiscourseNodeCandidate` → `SearchableNode`
   - `CandidateState` → `NodesState`
2. Fix commit: `getSearchableNodes` keeps only files whose `nodeTypeId` is one of the configured types, and the modal passes `plugin.settings.nodeTypes` with it in the effect's deps. The same commit removes the fallback.
3. Tests in `QueryEngine.test.ts`:
   - A configured type and an imported type (one with `importedFromRid`) are both kept.
   - An unknown id, an empty string and a non-string value are dropped.
   - Run on both the Datacore path and the vault-scan fallback.
4. Verification:
   - Unit tests, typecheck and lint.
   - In `testVault123` over CDP: a `nodeTypeId: bogus` note is gone; local nodes, imported nodes and tagged lines all still show.
   - Grep the bundle for `getSearchableNodes` first.
   - `dg-pr-adherence-check` before handoff.

**Done When** (to write into the ticket):
- Advanced node search lists only files whose `nodeTypeId` matches a configured node type (local or imported), whatever the type filter is set to.
- No "Unknown type" rows remain.
- The existing-node loader and its type are renamed so "candidate" means only tagged lines.
- Unit tests cover kept types (local, imported) and dropped ones (unknown, empty, non-string).

You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --slot 1 --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build]
```

It runs doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 vault locked, 3 marker missing.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- Slots come from `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It takes a JSON array or a comma list of plugin dirs or vault roots. `--slot N` is 1-based and defaults to 1.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved slot, the lock and the Obsidian state. If another live run holds the lock, it exits 2 and asks you to switch slot. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about competing `dev.ts`/esbuild watchers. Your own worktree's watcher counts too, if it mirrors into the same vault.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |

content.text:
I've made both changes on the branch, and the unit tests and the live run in Obsidian both pass. Notes with an unknown type no longer show up on either path, Datacore or the vault scan. Nothing is pushed yet and there's no PR.

**Commits**
- `07538474` renames the function and its type. `getDiscourseNodeCandidates` is now `getSearchableNodes`, and `DiscourseNodeCandidate` is now `SearchableNode`. The modal's loading state is now `NodesState`, with a `nodes` field. "Candidate" now only means tagged lines.
- `a716d937` is the fix. Both the Datacore query and the vault scan feed the same loop in [QueryEngine.ts:78](apps/obsidian/src/services/QueryEngine.ts:78). That loop now keeps a file only if its `nodeTypeId` is one of the types in `plugin.settings.nodeTypes`, local or imported.
  - The modal passes those types in and reloads when they change.
  - The "Unknown type" row is gone, along with `getFallbackNodeTypeBadge`. If a type is deleted while the modal is open, its rows drop out instead of showing a placeholder.

**Ticket:** I filled in Done When on ENG-2332.

**Verification**
- **Unit tests:** I wrote the new `getSearchableNodes` tests first. Before the fix they failed on both paths, with the `bogus` note in the results, which reproduced the bug. After the fix, all 77 tests pass. Typecheck is clean.
- **Lint:** no warnings on the lines I added. The two that show are on existing lines, `QueryEngine.ts:601,729`.
- **Live run in Obsidian** (`dgDevVault`, built from this branch, no type filter):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Notes with `nodeTypeId` set to `bogus`, an empty value, a local type and an imported type | Only the local and imported nodes are listed; no "Unknown type" row |
| "Show candidate nodes" turned on | The tagged line shows as a candidate; the bogus note stays hidden |

- **Caveats on the live run:**
  - `dgDevVault` has no imported node type, so I added one to the plugin's settings in memory for the run. It was never saved, and the scenario removed it afterwards.
  - The test notes are still in `dgDevVault/_verify/eng-2332-…/`; the harness never deletes notes.

**Before review:**
- `dg-pr-adherence-check` hasn't been run yet. I'll run it before we open the PR.
- The PR should say the leak started with ENG-2108's loader for existing nodes, not ENG-2272's tag scan.

**Possible addition to the CDP skill's gotchas table:** Datacore indexes a new note later than Obsidian's own metadata cache does. A scenario that creates notes and then opens the search modal has to wait for Datacore too, or new notes are randomly missing. That's what caused the one false failure I hit. Want me to add a line for it?
